description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/lib.rs:137

    pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler;

PROBLEM:
Re-exporting an upstream type at the crate root makes that upstream
type part of THIS crate's public API. If jmap-server later renames
ClosureHandler, changes its generic parameters, or cuts a major-version
bump (e.g., switching from `Box<dyn Future>` to `Pin<Box<dyn Future>>`
in HandlerFuture), this crate's public API is broken too — even though
nothing inside crate-jmap-contacts-server changed. Downstream consumers
get a transitively-broken API, and crate-jmap-contacts-server is forced
to cut a matching major-version bump to advertise the breakage.

The workspace AGENTS.md "Conventions list" reminds maintainers about
exactly this category of risk:
> "Re-exports from upstream crates that lock the major version."

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
That this crate's public API stability is independent of jmap-server's
public API stability.

ASSESSMENT:
ClosureHandler is workspace-internal (jmap-server is a sibling, also
0.x.y) so the version-skew risk is small in practice. But the precedent
matters: every extension-server sibling repeats this re-export, so
jmap-server is now de-facto part of the contracts of seven sibling
crates. A single ClosureHandler revision triggers seven major bumps.

The canonical sibling jmap-mail-server/src/lib.rs has the same
re-export. Workspace canonical-template propagation rule applies.

RECOMMENDED (any one of):
(a) Document this as deliberate API surface that intentionally mirrors
    jmap-server — add a `# Re-exports` doc-comment block noting the
    coupling explicitly.
(b) Wrap in a local newtype `pub struct ContactsClosureHandler<C>(...)`
    that forwards to jmap_server::ClosureHandler internally; this
    crate's API stays stable across upstream renames.
(c) Move the re-export behind a sealed/`#[doc(hidden)]` path so
    consumers cannot rely on it without explicit opt-in.

This is filed P3 because the coupling is intra-workspace and the
breakage risk is correlated (when jmap-server bumps, contacts-server
will bump anyway), but the contract implication is worth flagging now
before the crate publishes to crates.io.
title: pub use jmap_server::ClosureHandler — re-export locks this crate's API to upstream's major version
